The growth is therefore EXPECTED WORK for this change and a REGRESSION for any later one -- meta.frozen_for's v1.32 drift-detection reading is unchanged, it is only re-anchored. The fixture was re-captured cold (rm -rf .pio/build/native_trace_v131, then the same PLATFORMIO_BUILD_FLAGS="-D EPROM_V131_TRACE_DUMP" build-and-run-directly sequence the fixture header documents), and the suite's own two-drive determinism check passed against the pasted arrays. Entry COUNTS are unchanged (121/148/92) -- only 18 timing VALUES moved, which is why this bump is a blob_sha change with no arrays edit; the previous sha was 774a7e509ae021a13c4741d7eca9049bfb49f4df. RE-RECORDED A THIRD TIME by debug session w27c512-write-slow-3x (2026-08-22). Entry counts moved EPROM_V131_TRACE_PROTO_07 121 -> 131, EPROM_V131_TRACE_PROTO_08 148 -> 149, EPROM_V131_TRACE_PROTO_0B 92 -> 101 because that session replaced the per-BYTE program loop with a PASS-BATCHED one: the program-voltage route is asserted once per PASS (with one EPROM_VPP_SETUP_US and one EPROM_VPP_HOLD_US settle per pass) instead of once per programmed byte, and the scan pass that decides the next pass adds its own read-back traffic where the per-byte loop interleaved a verify read with each pulse. The per-byte cadence the previous arrays recorded WAS the defect this session fixed -- 1.568 s per 1024-byte block and 105.89 s for a 64 KiB W27C512 on a leonardo, against 29.71 s on the v2.x firmware (gh#36; gh#42 recorded 139.2 s); the pass-batched loop measures 33.51 s on the same rig, byte-exact. So, exactly as the Phase 145 re-record above describes for a different bug, this fixture was asserting a regression, and this growth is EXPECTED WORK for this change and a REGRESSION for any later one. Re-derived, never hand-edited: arrays and measured_entry_counts both come from the gate module's OWN _parse_arrays()/kind-column parse run against the live header, and blob_sha from `git hash-object test/native/avr/_shared/eprom_v131_expected.h` on the working tree before staging. measured_entry_counts was ALSO stale before this re-record -- it still held Phase 144's 91/115/59 merged figures after the Phase 145 re-record moved the arrays to 121/148/92 -- and is now consistent with the arrays for the first time (merged equals entries on all three). DEVIATION FROM THE ONE-COMMIT PROPERTY, stated rather than hidden: every earlier re-record landed the fixture and this inventory in the SAME commit so the identity gate never went transiently RED. That was not possible here. The fixture landed at 453a188 and was PUSHED to an open pull request (#55) before this gate's failure was discovered, so folding this record into that commit would mean rewriting published history under a live PR. This record therefore lands in a follow-up commit, recorded_at_head names the actual HEAD at recording time (273eedb) rather than this commit's parent, and the identity gate was legitimately RED for the two commits in between. Do not read recorded_at_head here as the parent-offset the earlier entries describe. meta.why_two_checks: A whole-file blob match alone cannot distinguish 'unchanged' from 'an array deleted together with the assertions that consumed it' -- both leave the remaining bytes identical to some other prior state's remaining bytes, so the per-array name+entry-count inventory is what makes a deletion visible.
meta.how_to_update: If this file legitimately changes, re-derive this inventory from the file with an independent parse (never hand-edit the numbers) AND state in the commit message which array changed and why -- never edit this JSON merely to make a surprise disappear.
meta.frozen_for: This record now arms the identity gate for v1.32 drift detection: a divergence from these three arrays (EPROM_V131_TRACE_PROTO_07/_08/_0B) is a regression to investigate, not expected work.
